programs.desc: Community Impact Program: In 2017 we made a bold goal to lift 15,000 household out of poverty by 2028. This takes a community wide effort of forming collaborations, agreeing on key measurements and tracking indicators with nonprofits, government, educators and businesses. 14,802 families have moved toward self-sufficency since we set this bold goal. Highlights in this area: Through grants from various collaborative partners, we offered Individual Development Accounts (IDA) which is a matched savings program where a participant builds assets for reliable transportation, education, debt reduction, start a business or steps towards home ownership. 184 individuals participated. The IDA program resulted in $1,318,908 of assets built. (source annual report). Our second cash assistance program served 190 families who received $500 a month for 12 months. Participants gained access to financial c

Community impact grants of $680,000 were distributed to various nonprofit agencies providing programs that help reduce poverty in Pierce County Washington. Grants are reviewed by staff and volunteers before being submitted to the United Way Board for approval. Capacity grants of $502,750 were given to 6 community partners providing finance and job coaches for our Centers for Strong Families (CSF) model. Individuals improve their financial condition, get better jobs and access to benefits. 1,000 individuals were served via CSF. 152 increased their income, 164 increased their net worth and 151 improved their credit score. The organization also distributed other grants of $361,066 that were donor designated to poverty reduction activities and $42,850 of board designated funds for emerging community needs.

211 is a free and confidential service that connects people with critical resources helping to stabilize individuals in Pierce, Thurston and Lewis counties. 211 became part of a statewide system in October of 2025. As a result of that we formed Access Pierce serving Pierce County where navigators who are experts in the areas of transportation, behavioral health, basic food, housing and early learning assist individuals to fill needs. 3,365 calls were answered in the last quarter of 2025. An example of an individual being helped by this program: A pregnant 18-year-old student faced a housing crisis and United Way staff responded immediately securing emergency shelter and guiding her through the process of qualifying for a low-income apartment. This resulted in stable housing for both mother and child.

Betye Martin Baker Human Service Center: Since 1995 our mission has been to offer other nonprofits significantly below market rent so they can put more money back into their missions. The service center is funded from tenant rents and capital campaign grants for major projects. Our aim is to have tenant rents 30% below market with the daycare at 70%. Reduced rents saved tenants approximately $343,327. Major upgrades in 2025 included the modernization of two elevators and adding disability access to the three entrances.

830841949.mission: The Open Doors mission is to ensure that homes will always be available for the most vulnerable and underserved people who are experiencing, exiting or at risk of homelessness.

programs.desc: Property NavigationThe Open Doors property navigation program is the core and vital front-line service that recruits properties and management companies for the Open Doors portfolio. Open Doors has continued to grow and expand. In 2024, our navigation team partnered with 185 participating property owners and management companies listing 742 multifamily communities as well as our 150 nonprofit collaborative partners. Open Doors placed more people and households in the Atlanta region in 2024 compared to any other operating year by securing rental homes for 1,223 people (731 households), bringing our total housed since 2014 to over 12,500 people.

TechnologyOpen Doors continue to showcase a large portfolio of available and affordable rental units through groundbreaking web applications. With our technology solutions, our partners report finding available units and obtaining approvals in under four weeks on average. Open Doors completed a refresh of our Property Listing App, including better filter and search functionality, an updated and refined user interface, and an inclusion of industry-standard property information and amenity listings.

Housing SupportsOpen Doors has applied the successful housing process developed for agencies working households exiting homelessness and applied it to a program called Housing Support Navigation. This program directly serves consumers who don't have case management support, but are experiencing housing insecurity. Through pilot programs with the Home Depot Foundation, Veteran Affairs at Fort McPherson, the City of Atlanta Housing Help Center, and other organizations, Open Doors provided "light-touch" housing navigation services. This includes unit location, lease execution, and post-placement supports to ensure housing stability. These pilot programs housed 133 people in 2024.

680429359.mission: Our purpose is to provide spiritual (Christian), medical, educational, and physical everyday-help to those in need in the Balkans (in and around Macedonia and the former republics that made up Yugoslavia).

programs.desc: PHYSICAL/EVERY DAY NEED SUPPORT - We send clothing and related needs on a weekly basis throughout the Balkans, via ship and air. These items are sent or taken to specific places and/or specific people for their needs and for distribution to others. For example, a box may be shipped to a hospital for distribution among children and/or needy adults. The greatest distribution is among refugees from different countries, including nations from the former Soviet Union and the Province of Kosovo. Thousands of pounds of clothing have been distributed among the people of the Balkans, including refugee Armenians, Kurds, Romanian, Turks, Russians and Ukrainians. In addition to clothing, funds are supplied especially among refugees and the elderly for their rent and heating fuel in the winter.We also provide nurturing and care for special need children who are not accepted in society.

SPIRITUAL HELP - We support or assist indigenous Christian workers in the various countries within the Balkan peninsula. We sponsor or co-sponsor 4-6 Vacation Bible Schools or youth camps each year.We supply Bibles and Christian literature as needed by these workers and / or churches. When designated, we have supported building of church structures or provided funds to repair and/or expand structures. We also have a ministry and conference center in Litochoro, Greece where Christian workers can be trained and renewed for service.

EDUCATION - We provide educational scholarships to over 200 children, youth and adults. For the last few years, we started a plan to educate and train as many national Christians as possible. Our hope is that many will go to seminary and serve in their homeland.It is generally for the following situations:- To fund education for students who would otherwise not be able to go to school; or,- To provide a Christian education to students; or,- To provide a vocational education so people can be trained to work.

MEDICAL SUPPORT - We provide vitamins and non-prescriptive medications on a regular basis. On occasions, prescriptive medications have been utilized through volunteer doctors. Also, on occasions, we have provided medical equipment and/or funds for same for hospitals in the Balkans.An on-going process is the caring for severe medical cases within the Balkans if the individuals can be properly treated. When they cannot be treated in-country, they are brought to an adequate facility in another country for medical treatment.

A national leader in championing contemporary American orchestral music, the Symphony has premiered and recorded works by many of today's most celebrated composers, earning 14 GRAMMY Awards and 27 nominations. The Nashville Symphony performs nearly 200 concerts annually, including free and low-cost education and community programs that collectively reach nearly 550,000 people of all ages across Middle Tennessee each year. Through broadcasts, recordings, and streaming, the Symphony extends its impact to an additional 13 million listen

Education & Community Engagement Programs: During the 2024-2025 season, the Nashville Symphony strengthened its commitment to accessibility and community connection through 278 free and low-cost education and community engagement programs, reaching nearly 36,000 students and adults. We expanded our presence beyond Schermerhorn Symphony Center through programs such as Music in My Neighborhood, Lunar New Year, and MLK: A Celebration in Song, bringing orchestral music directly into communities across the region. Music in My Neighborhood focused on the Antioch community, offering free ensemble performances, workshops, and family concerts in local schools and community centers. The third year of this community residency fostered cultural connection, neighborhood pride, and direct engagement with Symphony musicians. programs.desc: Summer Programs: North Littleton Promise (NLP) provided summer programming for elementary and middle school students through partners and at NLP. NLP sent 10 middle school students to Eagle Lake overnight camp, 20 elementary students to Eagle Lake on Location and 35 students to Beyond the 90, a local soccer camp. Additionally, NLP hosted a five-week summer day camp serving 53 students (40 elementary and 13 middle school). In the NLP camp, students engaged in literacy and math enrichment through project-based learning and hands-on activities. Programming also emphasized leadership development, communication skills, and faith formation in a community setting. Afternoon activities included field trips, guest speakers, and STEAM projects to promote engagement and enrichment.

After-School and Soccer Programs: NLP served 83 elementary, middle, and high school students through after-school programming. Students participated in academic support, enrichment activities, and faith-based programming while building relationships with trained volunteers. High school students also engaged in leadership development and peer community building. In addition, 67 youth ages 5-13 participated in NLP's soccer program across five teams. The program emphasized teamwork, skill development, and positive youth engagement.

Parent / Family Engagement and Resource Navigation: NLP facilitated multiple family engagement events to strengthen community connections, including a family STEM night, Easter event, soccer gatherings, summer picnic, and a Posada celebration. NLP also partnered with Doctors Care to train and support four parent leaders (promotoras) who provided health insurance education and resource navigation within the community, increasing access to information and support for families.
NLP added a second English class to the previously launched English and Spanish classes, and served 70 adult students in 2025.

In FY 2025, the NR program provided critical home repairs to 111 homes.

programs.desc: The Dream Experience - Program serves individuals living with chronic illnesses, intellectual or developmental disabilities or life-altering conditions. Collegiate Dream Teams - Groups of student leaders that are passionate about helping others in their community work alongside Dream On 3 to plan, market, fundraise, and ultimately fulfill the Dream Experience of an individual living with a life-altering medical condition. Teams consist of 15-20 students from each college. CDT members gain a wealth of real-world career and hands-on experience such as leadership development, team building, and community engagement all while helping someone in their community. The program develops work-related skills such as marketing, branding, public relations, social media, fundraising, donor relations, non-profit management, event planning, and more. We have worked with hundreds of students that have served on 47 CDT teams across various college campuses.

Jr. Dream Team - The Jr. Dream Team program helps student leaders plan, fundraise, and rally the school to support a fellow classmate living with a life-altering condition. Students work with faculty members and Dream On 3 staff to rally the entire high school in support of their Dream Recipient. Dream On 3 has found that when entire school and supporting community unite in the spirit of inclusion, the result is life-changing. We have worked with hundreds of students on 30 Jr Dream Teams across various high schools.

Alumni - Our Dream Kids are like family, so our relationship with them extends well past their initial Dream Experiences. Our alumni events are opportunities to reconnect with families and for them to connect with one another much like a family reunion. The Nicholas Thornton Scholarship Fundwas created in honor of our dear friend, Nicholas Thornton. Nicholas was a kind and loving 11-year-old boy who we lost in 2014. His life and values inspired us so much, we wanted his legacy to live on through the lives of our Dream Kids.

We also receive revenue from the facility rentals program for spaces available in the McGovern Centennial Gardens and Lott Hall. When the Commons opened in 2024, income opportunities were part of the operational plans. These include rental of the site's three pavilions, an improved Hermann Park Railroad stop, and the addition of a carousel as a new park amenity.

Initial services include basic wound care non-laboratory based testing and over the counter medication. For medical needs that quickly exceed our limited capabilities we work with community partners through referrals to address larger health needs such as womens health infectious disease emergency health needs and much more.

134353019.mission: The mission of 1IN6, Inc (1IN6) is to help men who have had unwanted or abusive sexual experiences live healtheir, happier, lives.

programs.desc: In the fourteen years since it was founded, 1IN6 has become a leading voice in the anti-sexual violence movement and a trusted resource for male-identifying survivors and their loved ones, as well a clinicians looking for research-based, trauma-informed information. 1IN6 helps to move these men from isolation into active recovery by providing accurate and compassionate information, inspiration, and support.Research indicates that the way masculinity is internalized often leads male survivors to repress their trauma and delay recovery. Moreover, the social stigma and silence around the issue of male sexual trauma results in a lack of awareness, which is a barrier to seeking help. The emotional impact of delaying recovery can systematically ripple out to every area of the survivors life, and th elives of those in his community. Men who do not get help risk exposure to greater physical heal

The clinical soundness of 1IN6s services, combined with the breadth and accessibility of our programming, has enabled us to develop strong collaborative relationships with a broad spectrum of leaders and organizations in the anti-sexual violence field. As a result, weve been able to effectively promote a trauma-informed understanding of mens coping strategies in fields as diverse as education, criminal justice, substance abuse, homelessness, child welfare, and mental and phycial health. We have also become a respected participant in national and international conversations about sexual abuse and assault.

Our trainings, many of which we have also made available in web-based formats, provide professionals an opportunity to enhance their knowledge and skills to effectively provide services for male survivors and those who care about them. Our awareness campaign, The Bristlecone Project, offers hope through stories, photographs, and videos of men who have reclaimed their lives after sexual abuse or assault.

The 1IN6 website (www.1IN6.org) is the worlds most thorough online resource (in english and spanish) for the tens of millions of men in the United States who have had unwanted or abusive sexual experiences, and for the loved ones and professional providers who care about them. 1IN6s direct services include our 24/7 online helpline and our weekly online support groups, which offer men safe, ananymous ways to access help.

851875789.mission: American Moment creates educational web content and publications, hosts educational conferences, develops a personnel database to connect students and young professionals with new and existing conservative institutions, and coordinate with existing campus and youth organizations with respect to educational initiatives and events.

programs.desc: Events - American Moment hosts over a dozen events per year ranging from family-friendly networking parties to professional development workshops to private salon dinners. Whatever the format, these events help those looking to join a larger network of like-minded individuals who support strong families, a sovereign nation, and prosperity for all, learn about professional best practices, find new opportunities, and build influence.

Fellowship for American Statecraft - American Moment organizes and pays accepted Fellows $3,000 per month for the summer and places them at an internship either on Capitol Hill or in the public policy non-profit sphere in Washington, D.C. The stipend is designed to be livable and not require outside housing supplementation, and Fellows are placed with American Moment allies to develop on-the-job skills and key early career credentials.

Web Content//American Moment Studios - American Moment Studios is the content generation arm of American Moment, bringing digestible visual and written content to a mass audience. Moment of Truth is American Moments original podcast production geared toward young people with an interest in policy and politics where young minds can engage with the best of what is being said and discussed in the conservative movement, keeping them up to date on the straight and narrow. Each episode features a guest at the top of their field discussing how they achieved their prominence, what they believe in, and what the best path forward for our nation is.

Coalitions - With an eye toward the future, we have created and maintained an internal database of vetted young people, including detailed notes on a given individuals background, policy expertise, interests, professional history, connections, worldview, and influences. As a result, when potential employers contact American Moment for personnel recommendations, we quickly can present them with viable candidates, making their hiring process simpler and augmenting our influence. This process is achieved through extensive interviews with young people who are looking to get involved or grow their influence. In these meetings, American Moment ascertains an individual?s historical and contemporary influences, their fluency on key policy issues, the states they have ties to, and the sort of work they are interested in pursuing.

programs.desc: TEXAS OFFICE FOR REFUGEES - Catholic Charities Fort Worth has served as the Replacement Designee for Refugee Support Services programs for Texas since 2021. The five-year commitment as Replacement Designee will end in September 2026.

REFUGEE SERVICES - These services encourage economic self-sufficiency by incorporating employment services, case management, financial assistance, language training, and community involvement to secure employment and preclude accessing cash assistance. These services offer employment training and coaching and placement services for refugees, asylees, Special Immigrant Visas (SIVs), victims of trafficking, refugees from Afghanistan and Ukraine, and Cuban parolees.

SOCIAL ENTERPRISES - The goal of our Catholic Charities social enterprises is to provide key services needed by the community while generating a surplus for Catholic Charities to grow services in other areas. Our social enterprises of Transportation and Immigration services provide those critical services for the community while our Dental Clinic addresses the dental needs of low income, uninsured, individuals and families.

WORKFORCE AND EDUCATION SERVICES - Several programs provide individuals with the resources and opportunities needed to obtain a living wage employment, including educational opportunities in targeted industries, and job placement services. Comprehensive support services are provided to low income students with the goal of helping them persist in school and obtain their degree. Services are targeted at helping students overcome obstacles outside of the classroom which might otherwise result in the student having to drop out of college. FAMILY SERVICES - These programs are designed to support the structure of a healthy family by offering free health assessments, pregnancy through early childhood education, and other support to strengthen families. programs.desc: CHILD EDUCATION -CHILD EDUCATION PROGRAMS INCLUDE THE EARLY HEAD START AND HEAD START PROGRAMS.THE EARLY HEAD START PROGRAM IS A FEDERALLY FUNDED, EARLY CHILDHOOD PROGRAM, CREATED TO BREAK THE CYCLE OF POVERTY BY PROVIDING SERVICES TO CHILDREN FROM LOW-INCOME FAMILIES. HOME VISITORS COME INTO THE HOME WEEKLY TO PROVIDE FAMILY SERVICES AND WORK WITH PARENTS AND CHILDREN ON ACTIVITIES BASED ON THEIR CHILD'S AGE AND FAMILY NEEDS.THE HEAD START PROGRAM PROVIDES PRESCHOOL SERVICES AND SOCIAL SERVICES FOR PARENTS OF CHILDREN AGED 3-5 YEARS OLD. THE ENERGY ASSISTANCE PROGRAM PAYS A PORTION OF A CLIENT'S WINTER HEATING BILLS. SUMMER COOLING ALSO PROVIDES AIR CONDITIONERS OR UTILITY BILL CREDITS IN SUMMER MONTHS, DEPENDING ON A FAMILY'S SITUATION. THE ENERGY ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS ASSIST A CLIENT WITH A ONE-TIME BENEFIT THAT IS APPLIED TO THEIR WINTER HEATING BILLS. SUMMER ASSISTANCE IS BASED ON WHETHER THERE ARE FUNDS LEFT FROM THE HEATING SEASON. PROGRAM YEAR 2021 ONLY ALLOWED FOR SUMMER CRISIS BENEFITS TO BE AVAILABLE TO THE MOST VULNERABLE POP

RENTAL UNITS ARE REQUIRED TO PASS A HOUSING QUALITY STANDARDS INSPECTION. GENERALLY, A FAMILY RECEIVING ASSISTANCE PAYS AT LEAST 30 PERCENT OF ITS MONTHLY ADJUSTED GROSS INCOME FOR RENT AND UTILITIES. THE PERMANENT SUPPORTIVE HOUSING PROGRAM PROVIDES PERMANENT HOUSING IN CONJUNCTION WITH SUPPORTIVE SERVICES TO HELP HOMELESS PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES AND THEIR FAMILIES. HOUSING VOUCHERS HELP PAY A PORTION OF THE FAMILY'S RENT AND ARE DESIGNED FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE HOMELESS AND DISABLED. CLIENTS MUST BE HUD DEFINED HOMELESS AND DISABLED. 261636099.mission: TO ACCELERATE SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY TO ELIMINATE SUFFERING AND DEATH DUE TO MELANOMA

programs.desc: THE MELANOMA RESEARCH ALLIANCE FOUNDATION ("MRA") SUPPORTS AMBITIOUS AND INNOVATIVE RESEARCH PROJECTS, SELECTED THROUGH PEER-REVIEW PANEL(S) AND INITIATED BY INDIVIDUAL SCIENTISTS AND SCIENCE RESEARCH TEAMS, TO PREVENT, DETECT AND TREAT MELANOMA. MRA CONVENES WORLD CLASS, CROSS-DISCIPLINARY GROUPS OF EXPERTS POSSESSING CLINICAL AND SCIENTIFIC EXPERTISE TO DEVELOP A RESEARCH AGENDA THAT WILL PROVIDE INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS TO CRITICAL RESEARCH ISSUES LEADING TO MORE EFFECTIVE PREVENTION, EARLIER DETECTION AND BETTER TREATMENTS FOR MELANOMA. MRA MAKES GRANTS TO DOMESTIC AND FOREIGN RESEARCH UNIVERSITIES, MEDICAL SCHOOLS, AND NONPROFIT MEDICAL RESEARCH ORGANIZATIONS DIRECTLY INVOLVED IN DETERMINING THE CAUSES AND CURES OF MELANOMA ON THE CONDITION THAT SUCH RESEARCH BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY.

THE MRA OPERATES A PATIENT ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM THAT SUPPORTS INCREASED AWARENESS OF MELANOMA IN GENERAL, AND OF PREVENTION, DETECTION AND TREATMENT OPTIONS SPECIFICALLY. THE PATIENT ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM ALSO PROVIDES EDUCATION ABOUT AND PROMOTION OF CLINICAL TRIALS AND A PATIENT REGISTRY FOR RARE MELANOMAS. THE PATIENT ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM INCLUDES DEVELOPMENT AND DISTRIBUTION OF EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS, THE PROVISION OF EDUCATIONAL FORUMS, A CLINICAL TRIAL NAVIGATOR FOR PATIENTS AND AN ON-LINE PATIENT COMMUNITY.

581287799.mission: TO HELP ABUSED CHILDREN OVERCOME THEIR EXPERIENCES AND REBUILD THEIR LIVES.

programs.desc: CHILD ENRICHMENT'S CHILD ADVOCACY CENTER (CAC) IS ACCREDITED BY THE NATIONAL CHILDREN'S ALLIANCE AND THE ADVOCACY CENTERS OF GEORGIA. THE CAC PROVIDES THERAPEUTIC SERVICES TO HELP CHILDREN RECOVER FROM THE TRAUMA AND TORTURE OF CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE. ALL SERVICES ARE PROVIDED FREE OF CHARGE TO CHILD VICTIMS AND THEIR NON-OFFENDING FAMILY MEMBERS. FORENSIC INTERVIEWING OF CHILDREN SUSPECTED OF HAVING BEEN SEXUALLY ABUSED AND EXPERT COURT TESTIMONY ARE PROVIDED WHEN ALLEGED PERPETRATORS ARE CHARGED WITH CRIMES AGAINST CHILDREN. CHILD ENRICHMENT'S CHILD ADVOCACY CENTER HAS BEEN SERVING ABUSED CHILDREN FREE OF CHARGE SINCE 1986.

CHILD ENRICHMENT'S COURT APPOINTED SPECIAL ADVOCATE PROGRAM (CASA) IS ACCREDITED BY BOTH THE NATIONAL AND GEORGIA COURT APPOINTED SPECIAL ADVOCATES ASSOCIATIONS. CASA REPORTS DIRECTLY TO JUVENILE COURT JUDGES ABOUT THE SAFETY, LIVING ARRANGEMENTS, SCHOOLING AND HEALTH COMPONENTS OF CHILDREN WHO HAVE BEEN REMOVED FROM THEIR PARENTS DUE TO ABUSE OR SEVERE NEGLECT. CASA ADVOCATES FOR ABUSED CHILDREN, SO THAT JUDGES CAN MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ABOUT SAFE AND PERMANENT PLACEMENTS. CASA RECRUITS, TRAINS AND SUPERVISES COMMUNITY VOLUNTEERS TO SPEAK UP FOR CHILDREN'S RIGHTS AND SAFETY. CHILD ENRICHMENT'S CASA PROGRAM HAS BEEN PROVIDING SERVICES FREE OF CHARGE TO CHILDREN SINCE 1995.

430666759.mission: DISCOVER/SHARE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT PLANTS AND THEIR ENVIRONMENT IN ORDER TO PRESERVE AND ENRICH LIFE.

programs.desc: HORTICULTURE: THE GARDEN'S HORTICULTURE PROGRAM DEVELOPS PLANT COLLECTIONS AND MAINTAINS LANDSCAPES FOR DISPLAY, HOME GARDENING DEMONSTRATIONS AND INFORMATION DISSEMINATION, AND IN SUPPORT OF RESEARCH AND EX-SITU CONSERVATION. THE GARDEN'S SEED BANK, LOCATED AT OERTLI FAMILY HARDY PLANT NURSERY, HOLDS 40 PERCENT OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI'S NATIVE FLORA. OUR PLANT COLLECTIONS INCLUDED 17,242 TAXA AND 9,141 SPECIES. THE GARDEN'S 79 ACRES FEATURE INDOOR AND OUTDOOR PLANT DISPLAYS THAT ATTRACTED 1,047,438 VISITORS IN 2025. HOME GARDENERS FROM AROUND THE WORLD REGULARLY USE THE GARDEN'S ON-SITE AND DIGITAL RESOURCES. THERE WERE MORE THAN 22.5 MILLION VIEWS OF GARDENING WEB RESOURCES IN 2025.

SCIENCE: THE MISSOURI BOTANICAL GARDEN IS A WORLD LEADER IN PLANT DISCOVERY AND PLANT CONSERVATION AROUND THE WORLD. IN 2025 GARDEN SCIENTISTS DISCOVERED MORE THAN 200 NEW PLANT SPECIES, WHICH IS ROUGHLY 10 PERCENT OF ALL NEW PLANTS DISCOVERED EACH YEAR WORLDWIDE. OUR HERBARIUM, WITH 8 MILLION SPECIMENS INCLUDING NEARLY 2 MILLION DIGITIZED SPECIMENS, IS AMONG THE LARGEST AND SERVES AS A GLOBAL DATABASE OF PLANTS USED TO MAKE EVALUATIONS ON CONSERVATION STATUS. BY KNOWING WHAT PLANTS ARE THREATENED, WE CAN IDENTIFY AREAS OF HIGH CONSERVATION VALUE WHERE PROTECTING LANDSCAPES MAY SAVE THREATENED SPECIES. THE GARDEN ALSO CONTINUES TO ADD ITS TROPICOS DATABASE, AND WORKS WITH PARTNERS AROUND THE GLOBE TO DIGITALLY DOCUMENT ALL KNOWN PLANT LIFE THROUGH WORLD FLORA ONLINE.

EDUCATION: THE GARDEN TAKES SERIOUSLY ITS MISSION TO SHARE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT PLANTS AND THE ENVIRONMENT WITH PEOPLE OF ALL AGES. IN 2025 345,231 PEOPLE PARTICIPATED IN EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES LED BY THE MISSOURI BOTANICAL GARDEN, FROM COMMUNITY-BASED PROJECTS TO ON-SITE AND VIRTUAL CLASSES AND EVENTS TO YEAR-LONG PROGRAMS AND COMMUNITY-BASED PROJECTS. OF THIS NUMBER, 37,801 WERE PREK-GRADE 12 STUDENTS AND TEACHERS WHO CONNECTED WITH THE GARDEN IN WAYS THAT DEEPENED THEIR UNDERSTANDING AND APPRECIATION FOR PLANTS, NATURE, AND THE IMPORTANCE OF LIVING SUSTAINABLY. IN THE COMMUNITY, THE GARDEN IS A LEADER IN EDUCATING AND ACTIVATING THE PUBLIC TO STEWARD LOCAL LANDS AND WATERS, FROM CREATING MORE BIODIVERSE HOME LANDSCAPES TO HELPING STEWARD LOCAL PARKS, TRAILS, CREEKS, STREAMS, AND OTHER GREEN SPACE IN THEIR OWN COMMUNITY.

PUBLIC PROGRAMS: PUBLIC EVENTS SUCH AS THE BEST OF MISSOURI MARKET. THE BEST OF MISSOURI MARKET IS PART OF THE AMERICAN ARTS EXPERIENCE ST. LOUIS, AN ANNUAL CELEBRATION OF THE ARTS THROUGHOUT THE ST. LOUIS AREA.

programs.desc: During 2025 the Oaks Phase 1 house provided services to 12 new women. New residents are provided clothes shoes and hygiene and given assistance with ID and other needed documents. The program includes church bible studies 12 step program counseling anger management relapse prevention life skills boundaries exercise community service and G.E.D tutoring as needed. After the 5th month residents attend a job readiness program.

The women move to Phase 2 once they have become employed and begin working with a budget and credit repair counselor to identify and reach financial goals. in 2025 a total of 20 women participated in the Phase 2 program including seven who successfully completed the Phase 1 house and transitioned to the Phase 2 houses. Seven women graduated the program Phases 1 and 2 in 2025 and were all employed.

In August 2023 the Phase 3 house was opened to provide affordable housing and support to women who successfully complete Phases 1 and 2 of the program and choose to continue their education or skills training. Eight women participated in the Phase 3 program including five women who successfully transitioned to Phase 3 in 2025.

Our Executive Director and Program Manager spend one day each week inside prison visiting the women leading Bible studies and introducing them to the Oaks community so they know there is a place of stability support and faith waiting for them when they are ready. Our Executive Director serves as the Volunteer Coordinator for the Faith-Based Dorm at the Plane Unit where she and our Program Director facilitate the faith-based program provide discipleship and alongside our Facilities Director lead worship services. Through this ministry we serve approximately 200 women each year in the Faith-Based Dorm.

362837499.mission: MUSIC OF THE BAROQUE IS A PROFESSIONAL ORCHESTRA AND CHORUS EXCELLING IN THE PERFORMANCE OF WORKS FROM THE 18TH CENTURY AND BEFORE. THE ORGANIZATION ALSO EDUCATES 2,900 CHICAGO PUBLIC SCHOOL STUDENTS EACH YEAR THROUGH ITS 'STRONG VOICES' SINGING PROGRAM.

programs.desc: UNDER THE DIRECTION OF INTERNATIONALLY ACCLAIMED BRITISH CONDUCTOR DAME JANE GLOVER, MUSIC OF THE BAROQUE'S PROFESSIONAL CHORUS AND ORCHESTRA IS ONE OF THE LEADING ENSEMBLES IN THE COUNTRY DEVOTED TO THE PERFORMANCE OF WORKS FROM THE SEVENTEENTH AND EIGHTEENTH CENTURIES.MUSIC OF THE BAROQUE CONTINUED FULL-TIME LIVE PROGRAMMING OF CHORAL AND ORCHESTRAL CONCERTS WITH WORKS BY BACH, HAYDN, HANDEL, MOZART, AND OTHERS. LESSER-KNOWN WORKS ARE ALSO FEATURED AS MUSIC OF THE BAROQUE SEEKS TO EXPAND THE AWARENESS OF AND APPRECIATION FOR WORKS FROM THE RENAISSANCE, BAROQUE, AND EARLY CLASSICAL PERIODS. DEVOTED TO EXPANDING ITS AUDIENCE AND ITS REACH TO A WIDER, MORE DIVERSE POPULATION, MUSIC OF THE BAROQUE PRESENTED 18 PERFORMANCES OF 8 DISTINCT PROGRAMS AS WELL AS VARIOUS COMMUNITY CONCERTS AND EVENTS TO A TOTAL AUDIENCE OF OVER 20,000 PEOPLE.
